scope: Two narrowly stated classification relationships in data/research/jurisdictions.json: UK SIC 2007 41.10 versus NACE Rev.2 41.10, and NAICS Canada 2022 111110 versus US NAICS 2022 111110. This review does not establish a complete concordance or accounting equivalence.

relationships.relationship_type: parallel four-digit class identity under the stated editions
verified_facts: ONS Operation 2007 states UK SIC 2007 was effective 1 January 2008 and was revised in conjunction with NACE.
The same ONS page states the two systems remain identical down to and including the four-digit class level.

The ONS SIC 2007 manual's structure summary lists 41.10 as Development of building projects, and its explanatory note describes bringing together financial, technical and physical means for residential and non-residential projects for later sale.
The ONS explanatory note excludes building construction (41.20), architectural/engineering activity and project management (71.1), so the code match does not erase the activity boundaries.

source_records.locator: Operation 2007 page, paragraphs stating UK SIC 2007 effective 1 January 2008 and identity through the four-digit class level (page lines 59-66 in the reviewed rendering)
Summary of Structure, PDF page 42: Section F, division 41, group 41.1 and class 41.10; Explanatory Notes, PDF page 152: 41.10 includes development for later sale and excludes 41.20 and 71.1

limits: No claim is made for NACE Rev.2.1, later NACE editions, UK five-digit subclasses, or a six-digit/deeper crosswalk.
A classification identity says how an establishment activity is coded; it does not select an accounting framework, tax treatment or reporting policy.
Rights to reproduce publisher text remain unresolved/publisher-terms; only original short synthesis is retained here.

relationships.relationship_type: single six-digit code/name alignment; not a Canada-US crosswalk
verified_facts: Statistics Canada’s official NAICS Canada 2022 to ISIC Rev.4 table lists Canada 111110 Soybean farming and maps it to ISIC Rev.4 A0111*; the asterisk and table notes demonstrate why a correspondence table is not a complete equivalence claim.
The US Census 2022 manual marks the 111110 heading with T (Canadian, Mexican and US industries are comparable) and defines the US industry as growing soybeans and/or producing soybean seeds.

The Canada leaf inspected through the Statistics Canada 2022 classification display is 111110 Soybean farming and describes establishments primarily engaged in growing soybeans. The matching number/title and comparable marker support this one named pair, while the wording difference means the pair should not be represented as text-identical or as a full crosswalk.

The US manual cross-reference routes soybean/grain combinations that do not have one crop accounting for one-half of production to 111191, which is a material boundary for applying the US leaf and cannot be inferred for Canadian classification from the shared code alone.

source_records.edition: NAICS Canada 2022 Version 1.0 / ISIC Rev.4 correspondence
source_records.locator: Official table rows 24-27: row for 111110 Soybean farming -> A0111* Growing of cereals (except rice), leguminous crops and oil seeds; explanatory note Soybean farming
NAICS Canada 2022 hierarchy and 111110 leaf display; Canadian industry description for soybean farming (page last modified 2024-10-23)
Part II Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting, PDF page 79: 111110 heading with T comparable marker, definition, and soybean/grain combination cross-reference

limits: Verified only for the named 111110 soybean-farming pair; no claim is made for all six-digit industries, all versions, or a bilateral concordance.
Statistics Canada evidence is a Canada-to-ISIC table, not a US-to-Canada crosswalk. The US T marker is a comparability signal, not an accounting or legal equivalence finding.
NAICS classification does not determine accounting framework, ownership/control, tax, reimbursement or regulatory treatment.
Rights to reproduce publisher text remain unresolved/publisher-terms; only original short synthesis is retained here.
